Mechanism: the median prefilter (`_median`, BOX_MEDIAN_WINDOW_SECS = 0.1 → 5 frames @ 50fps) exists to reject a short, large excursion in the box series. A 1-2 frame FighterTracker identity swap IS such an excursion, so the box series gets silently repaired while the keypoints — which nothing smooths — keep the swapped values. The stored `fighter_frames` row then has one fighter's box around the other fighter's skeleton.

Measured 2026-08-30 on the DB (docker exec fight_ai psql -U admin -d fight_ai): the skeleton's torso centre (mean of confident COCO joints 5/6/11/12) falls outside its own stored box on 585/71177 rows (0.82%) for fight 52 and 474/76606 (0.62%) for fight 54. A clear worked example is fight 52 frames 57302-57303, where corner 1's shoulder x jumps 1245 → 68 → 630 → 1242 while its box sits still at x≈1216-1280.

This matters because keypoints are the training signal for the planned skeleton action model (plan/04-stage2-model.md) — a mislabelled skeleton is worse than a missing one, and it is invisible because the box looks correct.

There is already a `_same_person(bbox, keypoints)` helper in box_smoothing.py that detects the condition (it currently only guards the new skeleton-floor step from acting on a mismatched pair). It does not repair anything.

Decide and implement a repair. Options worth weighing: detect the excursion before the median filter and swap the keypoints along with the box; or mark such rows so downstream export can drop them; or leave the box unsmoothed on those frames so box and skeleton stay consistent. Note the root cause is the tracker swap itself — see the memory notes tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches and corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps — so this is mitigation, and the fix should not pretend otherwise in its comments.

Follow ai/CLAUDE.md conventions: thresholds go in models/constants.py, and the module docstring must be corrected since it currently states this cannot happen. Validating needs a pipeline re-run (XL pose over the whole video), so also verify by replaying the new logic over the stored rows in Postgres first.

    if len(pts) < 2: return None
    return (sum(p[0] for p in pts)/len(pts), sum(p[1] for p in pts)/len(pts))

def outside_by(box, c):
    """How far the point lies outside the box, as a fraction of box diagonal."""
    dx = max(box[0]-c[0], c[0]-box[2], 0.0)
    dy = max(box[1]-c[1], c[1]-box[3], 0.0)
    diag = max(1.0, ((box[2]-box[0])**2 + (box[3]-box[1])**2) ** 0.5)

`track_fighters()` emits the raw detector box on every matched frame and
nothing at all on a frame the detector missed, so the boxes reaching the
annotation overlay jitter in position and size and blink out on dropped
detections.  Both are worst during a clinch, where heavy mutual occlusion is
exactly where the detector's box extent is least certain.

This is a post-process over the finished track dict rather than a change to
FighterTracker.  Because the pipeline is offline the whole sequence is
available at once, so the filter can be zero-phase — centred on each frame,
introducing no lag — which a causal online filter inside the tracker could not

-be.  Boxes and skeletons both arrive from the XL pose model already paired, so

+be.  Boxes and skeletons both arrive from the XL pose model already paired —
+but smoothing moves the box and nothing moves the keypoints, so the pairing is
+something this module has to actively preserve rather than something it gets
+for free.  Pass 5 is what preserves it.
-Three passes per track, in order:
+Five passes per track, in order:
+  4. Drift check — when the filtered box has been carried off its own
+     skeleton, the filtered value is discarded for that frame and the observed
+     box is used instead.  See below; this runs before the floor so the floor
+     is always applied to a box that belongs to its keypoints.
+
+  5. Skeleton floor — the box is unioned with this frame's own confident
+     keypoint hull, so smoothing can settle a box but can never crop it below
+     the joints the pose model actually saw.
+
+Step 4 exists because steps 2 and 3 cannot tell a *punch* from an *outlier*.
+Both are a brief, large excursion in w: an extended arm reaches its apex for
+2-4 frames at 50fps, and a 5-frame median filter is built to delete exactly
+that.  Measured on fight 52 (DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA_3) before this step existed, a
+confident wrist landed outside the stored box on 10.2% of frames, by a mean of
+35px and a p90 of 83px — and a wrist moving fast (top decile, i.e. mid-strike)
+was 3-4x likelier to be outside than a slow one, 5.9-7.1% vs 1.7%.  The box
+was therefore least correct precisely on the frames the whole system exists to
+capture.
+
+Step 4 exists because passes 2 and 3 can move a box *off the person it
+describes*, which detaches it from its own skeleton.  The filters act on the box
+series alone; nothing smooths the keypoints, so any displacement the filter
+applies is a displacement between a box and a skeleton that arrived together.
+The median prefilter is the sharp edge of this: it exists to overrule a short,
+large excursion, and a frame where the tracker briefly put a different person in
+this slot *is* such an excursion — so the box gets quietly pulled back onto the
+slot's trajectory while the keypoints stay with the person the detector actually
+found.  The stored row then shows one fighter's box around another's skeleton,
+and it is invisible in the overlay precisely because the box looks right.
+
+Measured on the stored rows of fights 52 and 54: the skeleton's torso centre
+falls outside its own box on 585/71,177 (0.82%) and 474/76,606 (0.62%) of rows.
+The shape of that population is what decides the repair:
+
+  - It is overwhelmingly **one-sided** — only 23 and 14 of those frames have
+    *both* fighters' rows mismatched.  So this is not mostly a clean two-fighter
+    identity swap that could be undone by exchanging the two slots' labels;
+    exchanging labels would address about 4% of it.
+  - Displacements run from marginal to gross: median 0.15 box diagonals outside,
+    p90 0.65, max 3.65.
+  - Runs are short — 80% and 93% of runs last 1-2 frames, the exact length the
+    5-frame median absorbs.
+
+The repair is therefore to **discard the filtered box** on those frames rather
+than to try to reconstruct the identity.  The observed box is guaranteed to hold
+its own skeleton — they are two outputs of one pose detection — so falling back
+to it restores the pairing by construction, for every cause, without this module
+having to diagnose which one applied.  It costs smoothing on <1% of frames.
+
+Two things it deliberately does not do.  It does not repair the *identity*: when
+the tracker put the wrong person in this slot, the row afterwards holds that
+person's box and that person's skeleton, consistently, and still under the wrong
+slot id.  That is the tracker's error and it is left where it can be seen —
+which is the second point: reverting makes the box jump on the overlay again,
+so a labeller watching the fight sees the glitch instead of a plausible-looking
+box hiding a mislabelled skeleton.  The root cause is upstream, in how
+FighterTracker resolves identity at a camera cut or in a clinch.

+fight 52's rows and 0.43% of fight 54's would be reverted, and everything left
+below the threshold is within 0.05 diagonals of its box.  The three fights
+processed before this module existed sit at 0.03-0.08%, which is consistent with

+predate the XL-pose box and had their keypoints IoU-matched to their boxes,
+which forced an overlap by construction.

+briefly engulfs both fighters or collapses onto a limb still *contains* its own
+skeleton, so it fails no drift test and the median goes on rejecting it as
+before.  Only boxes carried off their own person are reverted.

content.text:
Done. The data pushed me away from the repair I'd have guessed at.

## What the measurement changed

I checked the shape of the mismatch population before picking a fix, and the assumption in the brief — that these are two-fighter identity swaps — turns out to describe only a sliver of it:

- **It's overwhelmingly one-sided.** Only 23 of fight 52's 562 mismatched frames, and 14 of fight 54's 460, have *both* rows mismatched. A clean tracker swap crosses both slots, so exchanging the two slots' labels would have addressed about **4%** of the problem. That option is out.
- Displacements run marginal to gross: median 0.15 box diagonals outside, p90 0.65, max 3.65.
- Runs are short — 80% and 93% last 1–2 frames, exactly what a 5-frame median absorbs.

## The repair

Discard the filtered box on those frames rather than try to reconstruct identity. **The observed box is guaranteed to hold its own skeleton** — they're two outputs of one pose detection — so falling back to it restores the pairing by construction, for every cause, without the module having to diagnose which one applied.

New pass 4 (`_skeleton_drift`), running *before* the skeleton floor so the floor always acts on a box that belongs to its keypoints. `det["bbox_xyxy"]` is still the observed value at that point in the loop, so the fallback needs no snapshot. `BOX_SKELETON_DRIFT_RATIO = 0.05` box diagonals, set below the body of the measured distribution while ignoring cases where the torso centre is a few pixels past an otherwise-correct edge.

This also **subsumes `_same_person`**, which is now removed. That helper skipped the floor on mismatched pairs; reverting first means the pair is always consistent, so the floor no longer needs a guard — and the pathological case I'd seen (a box stretched 22× across both fighters) can't arise.

Two things it deliberately doesn't do, both documented in the module: it doesn't repair identity — a row afterwards holds one person's box and that same person's skeleton, still under the wrong slot id — and reverting makes the box **jump on the overlay again**, so the tracker's error is visible to a labeller instead of hidden behind a plausible-looking box. Root cause stays upstream.

The drift check and the median prefilter aren't in tension: a box that engulfs both fighters still *contains* its own skeleton, so it fails no drift test and the median goes on rejecting it.

## Verification

**End-to-end replay** of detection → tracking → smoothing over real frames 57250–57360, old logic vs new — this reproduces your worked example exactly (slot 1 box at x≈1216–1280 with its shoulder at x=68, drift 3.65 diagonals):

| | rows off their own skeleton | worst drift |
|---|---|---|
| old | 22 / 205 | 3.65 diagonals |
| new | **0 / 205** | 0.05 |

At frame 57303 the new output puts slot 0's box at x 1217–1280 with its shoulder at 1242 — box and skeleton together, and the swap now showing as a box jump.

**Synthetic test** reproducing the mechanism in isolation: with the check disabled, the box sits at x 55–135 while the shoulder is at 680 (drift 1.88); with it on, drift 0.00. The punch-floor regression still passes with zero spurious reverts on a clean track.

**DB replay** over all five fights sizes the blast radius: 0.56% of fight 52's rows and 0.43% of fight 54's would revert, everything left below threshold within 0.05 diagonals. Fights 31/42/44 sit at 0.03–0.08% — consistent with smoothing being the cause, though I noted in the docstring it isn't proof, since those predate the XL-pose box and had keypoints IoU-matched to boxes, forcing overlap by construction.

The docstring's false claim is gone, replaced with what actually holds: the pairing is something this module has to actively preserve, not something it gets for free.

Changed: [box_smoothing.py](ai/video_processing/fighter_tracking/box_smoothing.py), [constants.py](ai/models/constants.py). Not yet re-run, so the DB still holds the old rows. One note — Postgres was down again when I started; OrbStack needed a manual start.

content.text:
Not really — ViTPose is a two-stage top-down model (needs a separate person detector first, then a transformer pass per detected person), which makes it noticeably slower than YOLO-pose even in its smallest variant. ViTPose-B can get close to real-time on a strong GPU for just a couple of people, but it wasn't built for that and you'd be fighting the architecture the whole way.

If live is genuinely the target, RTMPose is the better fit — it was explicitly designed for real-time multi-person pose and reportedly holds most of ViTPose's accuracy at a fraction of the latency, with CPU-viable variants too.

One thing worth flagging: this pipeline is currently offline/batch — `main.py` processes recorded video files start to finish, not a live feed. Swapping toward a "live" model would be a different deployment shape, not a drop-in replacement. Is that actually the direction you're considering, or was this more of a general question?
